title: Chicken Katsu
subtitle: Japanese breaded chicken cutlet with curry sauce
excerpt: Japan's best-loved comfort dish: a thin chicken breast, pounded flat, coated in golden panko breadcrumbs, and fried until crunchy, served with a sweet, mildly spiced katsu curry sauce poured over rice.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken katsu (katsuretsu, from the English 'cutlet') is a variation of the tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) that arrived in Japan with Western cuisine in the Meiji period. The Japanese adapted the technique to create an extraordinarily consistent breaded cutlet that differs from its European counterpart chiefly in the use of panko (Japanese breadcrumbs, which are coarser and drier and produce a lighter, crispier coating). The katsu curry sauce is a derivative of the Indian curry that was introduced to Japan via the British Royal Navy, simplified and sweetened into the distinctive golden sauce that accompanies the dish. Wagamama popularised the dish in the UK in the 1990s. The sauce can be made in advance and refrigerated; it improves overnight.

content.text: Butterfly the chicken breasts and pound to an even 1 cm thickness; uneven thickness means part of the chicken overcooks while the thickest part is still raw. Panko is essential: fine dried breadcrumbs produce a dense, oily coating rather than a crisp one. The oil for frying must be at exactly 170°C; too hot and the panko burns before the chicken is cooked.

items.preparation: for the sauce; mixed with 2 tbsp cold water

content.text: Make the sauce: cook the onion, carrot, and garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil for 10 minutes. Add the curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Add the stock, soy sauce, and honey. Simmer for 15 minutes. Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer until thickened. Blend until smooth.
Season the chicken. Coat each breast in flour, then beaten egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs firmly to adhere.

Heat the oil to 170°C. Fry the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper. Slice thickly on the diagonal. Serve over steamed rice with the curry sauce poured over.
